messages:
maya: Heads-up — profiling shows a regression when we flip kernel-decider to prefer arch-optimized kernels for seqlen > 2048. RTT p50 up ~12% on a subset of long-chat workloads.
sam: Hmm, which path changed? kernel-decider config or driver handshake?
maya: kernel-decider picks now include an 'arch_pref' score; when it picks A100-optimized kernels for mixed batches we hit more KV cache misses.
cheng: That makes sense. We salt KV keys by model+driver_version currently. When kernel choice varies by seqbin we end up with different key patterns at runtime.
irene: Can you paste the sample key pattern?
maya: Sure: `kv:{model:v2}:{driver:v1.9}:{session:abc}:{seqlen_bin:>2048}:{kernel:cuda_fused}` vs the older `kv:{model:v2}:{driver:v1.9}:{session:abc}:{seqlen_bin:>2048}` — kernel was appended in the new autotuner.
sam: Adding kernel into the key smells like over-salting. It prevents reuse across kernel variants that are backend-equivalent for KV.
cheng: Right. But we added kernel to capture kernel-specific cold-start/warm metrics for autotuning. We could instead tag the metadata in the persistence layer while keeping the key stable.
maya: Two UX constraints: 1) we need to roll back keys on driver upgrade without O(N) invalidation; 2) we need to maintain correctness when a kernel variant uses incompatible KV layout.
irene: For (2) can we detect layout incompat at kernel registration time and flip to per-kernel namespaces only for incompatible ones? Compatible kernels share namespace.
sam: That would work. Also consider versioned namespace prefix like `ns:v2-stable/` and a small metadata index that maps namespace -> kernel hints. Perf-bot: autotune-alert: p50 latency regression detected on cluster:us-west-2 - grouping: long-chat - delta:+12% - implicated-change: kernel-decider:arch_pref-1.
cheng: Implementation sketch: keep key = `kv:{model}:{driver_hash}:{session}:{seqlen_bin}`. Keep a sidecar metadata table `kv_ns_meta:{namespace}` storing `kernel_whitelist`, `layout_hash`, `created_ts`. When a kernel wants to write, it checks metadata; if layout_hash mismatch -> write to a per-kernel namespace and emit a warning.
maya: How do we persist metadata across driver restarts and upgrades? We need atomicity guarantees so the runtime doesn't see partial writes.
sam: Persist to RocksDB with a simple compare-and-swap on namespace metadata. On driver upgrade we write a new driver_hash; readers will deterministically map to the correct namespace.
irene: What about invalidation? If we detect a kernel bug and need to invalidate keys for a namespace, do we delete keys or rotate namespace prefix?
cheng: Rotate prefix. Deleting is expensive. Namespace rotation: bump `ns_rev` in the `kv_ns_meta` and create a fresh namespace pointing to empty data. Old keys live until GC window.
maya: That solves quick invalidation. But we should avoid orphaning too many keys across frequent autotuner changes.
sam: Add cheap reference counters: per-namespace active_sessions count. If zero for >TTL, schedule GC. Also limit per-session new-namespace churn by hashing session->chosen_namespace with sticky fallback.
cheng: Also: batching heuristics interact. Batches that mix seqlen bins will prefer a neutral kernel, but our current kernel-decider was switching kernels mid-batch which forced cache misses. We should prefer kernel stability within a batch.
maya: Agreed — put a penalty in the kernel-cost function for switching kernels inside an active batch window. 
irene: Ops question — how do we rollout this change safely? Canary with small percent, monitor KV hit rate and p50. Deploy-bot: deploy plan queued: canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% if KV_hit_rate delta < -1% and p50 delta < +5%.
perf-bot: perf-check: simulated workload replay shows namespace-rotation + metadata sidecar reduces p50 regression to +1.5% and improves KV hit from 68% -> 82%.
sam: Nice. A few extra items: document the metadata schema, add an admin endpoint to force namespace rotation, and emit metrics: `kv.namespace_rev`, `kv.layout_mismatch_count`, `kv.namespace_gc_pending`.
maya: I'll draft an RFC with the sketches and timeline. Action items: maya -> write RFC; cheng -> prototype metadata sidecar; sam -> add kernel switch penalty; irene -> run canary plan.
cheng: I'll start a small prototype tonight, will push a 10-line shim to map keys and a test harness.
maya: Thanks. If anyone hits the regression in the wild, ping me directly.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy: kernel-decider:v2 -> 5% started.
